minor.comment: Transform-only animations on HTML elements are drawn every frame through a motion channel of their own, without waiting for the atomic commit, unless a step would change the panel's paint order
A transform animating on its own re-reads only what depends on the element's transform, not the rest of its computed style
Add paint order's layer model, the tree that orders a panel's layers and the half-plane test in a box's and a mark's materials, none of them used by a panel yet

Add the `paintOrder` panel option, off by default, which draws a panel in paint order: flat on its layers' planes, its layers ordered by a tree walked from the viewer, its boxes and text in one batch, and one depth quad over its root
Draw every panel in paint order by default; `paintOrder: false` keeps the lift for now

Draw every panel in paint order, its only model. Breaking: the `paintOrder` and `depthRank` panel options are removed, with the lift they chose between and the depth bias, and each panel's boxes and text now draw in its one batch

Add the paint-order draw count and draw bench, which compare a panel drawn in paint order with the lift
Share the box and text batches' instancing helpers, split measureTextCanvas out of generateTextTexture and add hasDepthTransform, with nothing drawn differently

minor.comment: A `fill` or `stroke` naming a paint server with a fallback colour, `url(#hatch) black`, is drawn in that colour in an SVG panel instead of as nothing

A change to a list's children restyles the list's siblings only when `:empty` may have flipped: when the list holds no element or text that it held before the observer flush. A log that drops its oldest row no longer restyles the rest of its panel, and an append after a framework's comment anchor stays narrow, while the first row into a list holding only a comment anchor now restyles the list's neighbours.

A ray now sends the pointer model a page expects: buttons on every event, the boundary events, pointercancel when a press becomes a scroll or a drag, the capture events with the Element.prototype wrap held only while a panel is up, a captured hand's moves off the panel's controls, and mouse events from one primary hand. In development, a press on content no ray targets is named once.
A captured hand's release takes its point from where the ray crosses the captor's panel, as its moves do, in place of 0, 0 off the panel

An `<svg>`'s content now draws in the first half of its content level, before the boxes drawn at that level, so a translucent box in front of the `<svg>` shows all of it rather than its earlier elements only.
Panel handles stay out of the scene until the panel or its loading frame is drawn, and draw after every panel so one behind them no longer covers them
The rows that leave an open panel are taken out of the scene at the commit and, under render(), taken down over the frames after it instead of in the commit's frame
A closed panel leaves the scene, the rays and the page at once, and under render() its objects are taken down over the following frames in the scheduler's leftover budget instead of in one long task
A row that leaves an open panel keeps what its reads said until its objects are taken down, so the panel no longer draws it again from DOM out of the document before the commit

A hand that disconnects, as every hand does when a session ends, lets go of what it held: the manager ends its presses as lost misses and leaves at once, so drag() and carry() let go and a panel cancels the pointer. A panel's data-xr-hover and data-xr-active are counted per hand, and the hover follows a captured pointer to its captor. The scene's keyboard goes when the session ends, the session button gives up focus once the session starts, and casting a ray, carrying and dragging make nothing per frame. carriedPose takes an optional pose to write into.

An author's attribute change now climbs the layout walk, so a class swap or `hidden` that resizes an element moves the boxes after it and resizes the panel. An inline style write that changes only properties that move no box, such as `transform`, `opacity` or a colour, still re-measures only the element's own subtree. The animation clock now treats the background properties and `outline` as paint, so an animated `background-image`, `background-position` or `background-size` restyles its element instead of re-measuring the panel.

A press on a field's label gives the field the keyboard, as a page focuses it, and such a label is a ray target whatever its cursor. The portal's own flag names come from one set of constants in portalRoot.js, and FOCUS_ATTRIBUTE is exported from @apendua/freedom and @apendua/freedom/page.
A panel option, depthRank, draws its batched boxes with a depth bias by paint rank, a prototype of item 10.2 of the architecture plan; off by default.
Keep each text run's raster at the step below the one its panel shows, so leaning back out of a step draws and uploads nothing
Keep a picture's texture idle after its last element lets go of it, within a 16 MiB budget, so a picture that comes back is drawn at once instead of loading again

Add outlines mode: enableOutlinesMode() outlines each panel element that changed at a commit, solid for a change the page made, dashed for one it caused elsewhere, dotted for an element the mirror measured again for nothing and grey for a write of what was already there, coloured by how often, and outlinesReport() lists what it counted
Draw a panel's text at the step above before the panel reaches it, and send its arrays to the GPU ahead of the crossing
SVG: draw a clip-path that names a <clipPath> of one <rect>, on the clip box a nested <svg> already uses

Geometry attributes inside an `<svg>` (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `rx`, `ry`, `d`, `points`, `dx`, `dy`, `rotate`, `transform`) now restyle only the element and its subtree, not its siblings, so a drawing that moves no longer restyles every shape for each one that changed.

SVG shapes other than <path> are built into a ShapePath directly instead of being written out as markup for SVGLoader to parse, so a shape whose numbers change every frame no longer parses a document every frame. A polyline's or polygon's points are read by SVG's grammar, so a list written `0, 0 10, 0` is no longer drawn with its pairs shifted. readShapeMarkup is now readShapeGeometry, returning the numbers.
SVG text in a font smaller than 64 units is laid out and drawn at a power-of-two multiple of its size, so its glyphs sit on the baseline the layout gave it on a high-DPR display such as a headset

A panel can take a hand's thumbstick as a mouse wheel: the thumbstickWheel option sends wheel to the element under the ray while the hand holds no button, for a page that zooms or pans on the wheel. Off by default.
playHapticAll plays one haptic effect on every input source of an XR session, and does nothing outside one, for a rumble that belongs to the scene rather than to one hand.

Keep every shader program freedom draws with linked for the life of the renderer, so that a panel mounted after the last of its kind has closed, a text bucket that grows, a loading frame and a panel's handle bars no longer link a program again after three deleted it

A stylesheet whose rules all start from classes, such as every sheet justdom's className writes, restyles only the panels those classes can reach instead of every panel on the page, so a keyboard opening no longer restyles and re-measures the whole scene
Add `enableThemingMode()`, which follows rule edits made through the CSSOM or the browser's developer tools by reading the document's rules on a timer
A ControllerHandle now carries ray, the line drawn down its target ray, so an app can hide the line while the hand is busy without taking the hand out of the raycast.
Upload a text or box batch's instance buffers only when a rebuild changed what they hold, rather than every buffer of every bucket on every rebuild
Draw a stepped box that is not opaque after everything the sibling it clears draws, so a box behind text, a caret, a list marker or a field's value never draws after it

patch.comment: Text in an inline element under a CSS transform wraps as it does on the page: the measurement clone is taken of the box its lines are laid out in, not of the inline parent, which has no width to wrap against
A press swallowed on an element that had gone is silent to its end: no release or click goes to a live control around it, and it ends the last press's say over didDrag.
A captured hand's gotpointercapture and lostpointercapture, and the crossings a release brings with its ray off the panel, say where the pointer is instead of 0, 0
Leave a panel's blockers out of the draw: they write neither colour nor depth, so each cost a draw call per eye for nothing
pointercancel, the leaves after it, the leaves of a lost hand and the crossings after a press that sent no pointerup say where the page last heard the pointer instead of 0, 0

A ray that leaves a panel, onto nothing or onto another panel, now sends its pointerout, pointerleave and the mouse's at the point the page last heard the pointer, instead of 0, 0; so do the crossings that bring a panel up to date for a hand over nothing on it.

Texts under a transform in one line box are measured in one shared copy of the box, kept until something it was copied from changes, rather than a copy each, so measuring a paragraph is linear in its size rather than quadratic, a portal mount included
A drag or a carry swallows a release only when it took the press the release ends, whatever enabled says in between; drag() and carry() share that release through createHold.

An inline style write of the offsets, sizes or margins of an element positioned absolute or fixed re-measures that element alone, since its box is out of the flow, so a scrollbar thumb moved on every scroll no longer re-measures the boxes around it.

A subtree that leaves a panel is let go of by the mirror at once, so nothing the panel hears before the commit measures it again; a checkbox's checked accessor is taken off when the last panel stops reading it; the SVG plugin no longer adopts templates itself

The interaction manager sends a press's end, completion and miss no further along its path than the start went, so a drag() or carry() taken out of the scene mid-press no longer leaks its release to what is behind it; createHold drops its set of taken starts.
An whose picture is an SVG is drawn on a canvas at its natural size before it is uploaded, since Chrome refuses to upload an SVG with no size of its own as a texture
Read the width and height attributes of a <use> or a nested <svg> when the browser computes them as auto, as Chromium 152 does, so a symbol is fitted to the size the <use> names
anchorToViewer leaves three on the reference space it requested when the runtime offsets spaces by NaN, as the Immersive Web Emulator extension's IWER does
anchorToViewer builds the anchor from the transform's matrix on a runtime that offsets by NaN otherwise, so it runs in full in the Immersive Web Emulator extension
An SVG element writes its matrix and its clip uniforms in one effect, so a panel that is not atomic no longer draws a moved element through the clip it had before the move

A box writes its place and its clip in one effect, so a panel that is not atomic no longer draws a moved box through the clip it had before the move; and an object the portal attaches to a new parent has its world matrix recomputed, so one that keeps its offset in its new parent is not drawn and hit where the old one put it
SVG shapes resolve percentage lengths against their viewport, and SVG text measures through the mirror's measurement clone and its one shared Range

minor.comment: A panel the page scales, on its root or above it, is measured at its layout size: every client rect goes through panelFrame.js and is divided by the scale of the root's chain, the ray's points are scaled back, a rotation, skew or flip on the chain, or a perspective above the root, warns once per root, and a window scroll or resize starts a new geometry generation

A panel forwards what rays do to its page from one listener on its container, in place of listeners on every element. The recorded event sequences are unchanged. Two cases they did not cover now behave differently: a control in a scrolling list that is no control, inside another control, now presses the outer control too; and a press of the trigger whose row's removal commits during the hold now ends with its release, so the control around the row hears the release, a page that cancelled its pointerdown hears mouse moves again, and a capture ends, while a grip that outlives its row the same way stays the panel's to its end, and its opening is felt. An element built outside any portal is a ray target and is no longer forwarded.

A panel that is always busy still loads and still updates: the pump takes the observer's records at the top of each tick, the animation clock is held while a panel loads, and a pump that has waited MAX_COMMIT_WAIT on a channel that will not empty sweeps it unbudgeted; one whose build the page keeps adding to for MAX_BUILD_WAIT builds what is queued and sweeps in one frame. A node the page adds and removes before the observer's records are read no longer counts as an arrival, and a row taken out, put back and taken out again in one flush is now taken down rather than left drawn.

A portal's container carries data-xr-busy while the animation clock samples or the pump has an update still to draw, so a harness can wait for the scene to catch up with the DOM before it photographs. The portal ignores an observer flush made only of its own container flags.

Clip a transformed element where its layout puts it, so a rotating element in a clipping parent is no longer cut differently at each angle

minor.comment: Mouse events a ray sends to a mirrored page carry the point it met as clientX and clientY
The grip on a mirrored element sends the page a contextmenu, and a mirror cache read before its node was adopted follows the node once it is

Positioned and transformed siblings are now stepped in depth in front of the earlier siblings they overlap, so a clock hand no longer vanishes into its dial and an earlier card's text and pin no longer show through a card laid over it; siblings that do not overlap stay level.

patch.comment: Text rewritten inside an inline element re-measures what follows it, so a caret after a prompt moves with every key even when the prompt keeps its size
A translucent card laid over another card now draws after it, so the other card's label shows through it tinted, as on a page, rather than disappearing where the card covers it

minor.comment: Draw CSS gradient backgrounds in panels: linear, radial and conic gradients and their repeating forms, laid out by background-size, -position, -repeat and -origin, baked into a shared ramp atlas so gradient boxes stay in the batch
The caret of the field being typed into blinks, solid again after each keystroke.

dom() and createPortal mirror an element the page already has: pass an HTMLElement (or a subscribable of them) to dom(), or root to createPortal, and the portal watches it where it stands instead of mounting into a container of its own, so an app with a flat interface adds an immersive session without building its UI twice.

Panels speak HTML drag and drop: a draggable="true" element picked up with the trigger sends dragstart, dragenter, dragover, dragleave, drop and dragend as a browser would, across panels, with a DataTransfer that honours dropEffect and effectAllowed
The drag ghost is a picture of what is dragged, rendered once at dragstart, where it was an outline

Panels can opt into being moved by the player with `draggable`; `carry()` keeps the tilt an object was taken with and takes `level: false` for the hand's whole rotation; `runFrame` runs a renderer's frame callbacks for tests; the keyboard is always draggable and its `draggable` option is gone.

An element's opacity now fades everything inside it, as on a page: boxes, text, a field's value and caret, and SVG shapes are drawn at the product of their own opacity and every ancestor's up to the panel's top

Draw list markers in panels for any element laid out as a list item, <li> and <summary> included: bullets and disclosure triangles, numbers in every common list-style-type, start, value and reversed, inside and outside positions on the item's first line, right-to-left markers, ::marker colour and font, and the item's own overflow clip

A panel follows every attribute written inside it, not a fixed list: an SVG shape's d, fill, points or transform bound to data is redrawn when it changes, and an app's own attribute selectors restyle. The portal's own data-xr-loading and data-xr-portal flags on the container are ignored.
The keyboard a field brings up follows the haptics of the panel it types for, with the hover on for its keys unless that panel turned it off by name, and silent for a panel with haptics: false.

Panels are felt: every control (an element with cursor: pointer) pulses the controller's motors when the trigger closes on it, and, where a panel asks for it with haptics.hover, when the ray arrives on it, once per arrival and not while the hand scrolls a list. PanelOptions and PortalOptions take haptics (hover, off by default; active; strength; flavor: tick, knock, buzz, key or a HapticFlavor of your own; false for none), spread one over the other like keyboard and loadingFrame; playHaptic drives a hand's motors for a scene's own haptics. Pointer events now carry the controller's inputSource and the registeredTarget their hit belongs to; enter and leave are per registered target (a ray drifting from a button's label onto its background is a pointermove, not a leave and an enter) and carry relatedTarget, the registered object the ray came from or went to. InteractionManager.addController takes a reader for what is driving the controller.

Add PanelOptions: scene-wide panel defaults (keyboard, loadingFrame, maxTextScale, atomic, opaqueToRays, priority, budget) set through render()'s panelOptions or withPanelOptions, with each panel's own options laid over them. A panel's keyboard option may now be partial or false. loadingFrame no longer accepts true: leave it out for the default frame, or pass false or an options object.

A press on nested clickable elements works as on a page: the innermost element is the target of the DOM events, sent once, every clickable element around it takes data-xr-active and hears its onPress, and the ray event stops at the outermost of them

A <g> under cursor: pointer is a ray target, so it is hovered and pressed with the shape the ray is on, and a .node[data-xr-hover] rect rule restyles the node. A registered object inside another is cast once, by the outer one's walk, and a pointerleave, a release and a grip's release reach every object their start went through, even once the object under the ray was taken out of the scene.

One keyboard for every panel in a render() scene, set once through panelOptions: it opens in front of the player at a constant size (placement, reach, drop, scale), stays put while typing moves between panels, can be moved by handles along its edges that show on hover (draggable), and follows focus like a page, staying up on Enter and going on a press anywhere but a field. KeyboardTarget gains field().
Restyle only the animating element for non-inherited animated properties, and add a createPortal atomic option to opt a panel out of whole-or-nothing updates

Portals now respect CSS visibility: a hidden element draws nothing of its own and takes no rays, while a descendant can show itself with visibility: visible. The portal container is kept out of sight by translating it off-screen rather than with visibility: hidden, which every element inside used to inherit; it is inert and aria-hidden, and says visibility: visible for itself so a page hiding its own content does not hide the panels.

Inline SVG in a portal, as a plugin: a new @apendua/freedom/svg entry point whose svgElements() draws <path>, <rect>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polyline> and <polygon> from their computed style -- fills with fill-rule, strokes with caps, joins, dashes and dash offsets (dots included), transforms, viewBox and preserveAspectRatio, opacity, display and visibility, clipping by the panel -- behind a general element-plugin seam (PortalOptions.plugins, RenderOptions.portalPlugins, PortalPluginsContext). An <svg> without the plugin is its CSS box and nothing inside it. The animation clock now follows SVG elements and classifies SVG paint properties, so a stroke-dashoffset animation samples one element rather than re-measuring the panel.
freedom/svg: an <image> inside inline SVG is drawn, as a textured quad under the shape's matrices
freedom/svg: markers on paths are drawn, and the portal follows SVG templates it does not build
freedom/svg: <use> and <symbol> are drawn, and a copy inherits the <use>'s styles
freedom/svg: a nested <svg>, a <symbol> and a <marker> clip their content to their viewports

SVG shapes under cursor: pointer are ray targets of their own: they forward hover, press and click to their element as a box does, follow pointer-events for which of fill and stroke a ray hits, and are clipped for rays as for drawing

SVG in portals, S4b: shapes keep their geometry in user space and transforms move onto the scene graph — the <svg> root's content group carries the viewport, each <g>, nested <svg> and shape its own transform — so a transform animation or a root resize is a matrix write; the clip follows through the clip matrix. box() gains a contentMatrix option.
SVG in portals, S4a: the clip patch (applyClip) takes an optional mesh-to-frame clipMatrix uniform, applied in the vertex shader; everything passes the identity for now, so nothing moves.
Draw SVG <text> and <tspan> in a portal, laid out by the browser in an untransformed copy and drawn as textured quads in user space

Text fields are mirrored: the value or placeholder drawn in the box, followed through input events and the value setter, with a caret while typed into. PortalOptions.keyboard takes a factory for the board's DOM; the portal mounts it below the panel when a field is pressed, types into the field through the exported typeIntoInput, and dismisses it on Enter, Escape, a background press or the field leaving. The portal handle gains size(), and fields carry data-xr-focus while typed into. RenderOptions.presentingOnly draws only while an immersive session is presenting, for a page that offers a session as an extra.

The keyboard in the room previews the field being typed into just above its keys: unmasked, in the field's own look (or preview.className), leaning toward the player by preview.tilt (15°), preview: false to leave it off. The caret of a field being typed into is placed by the ray's select press and dragged with it, the preview's going into the field; number and email fields keep a caret too. BoxOptions gain interactions; InputFocus gains placeCaret; PREVIEW_ATTRIBUTE is exported.

patch.comment: A box's border is drawn in the colour of the first side that has a border, so a one-sided border such as a bottom divider is drawn in its own colour rather than the text colour
A drag from one panel to another keeps the other panel's controls unhovered, and its ghost follows the ray onto whichever panel it is over
A press whose mousedown is cancelled after a drag is a click again, and the control a drag ends on is hovered on the next move

A controller three is not tracking (not yet connected, disconnected, or with its pose lost) points at nothing: getIntersection casts no ray from a hidden target ray space, for the hover and for presses, and the manager looks again when its visibility changes, so cursors and hovers go when a session ends and a press from a lost hand lands nowhere
